ingredientsCatalog.name: Ground Allspice
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Ground allspice is a potent spice made from the dried and ground berries of the Pimenta dioica tree. It is a versatile ingredient used in both sweet and savory dishes, known for its complex flavor that combines notes of cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, and black pepper. Also called pimento or Jamaican pepper, it is used in a wide variety of cuisines, from Caribbean jerk seasoning to European baked goods and Middle Eastern stews.  
Characteristics and flavor
Aromatic: It has a strong, warm, and earthy aroma. 
Complex flavor: It tastes like a combination of cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, and black pepper, which is where it gets its name. 
Origin: It comes from the dried, unripe berries of the Pimenta dioica plant, native to Central America, Mexico, and the Caribbean. 
Culinary uses
Savory dishes: It is used in stews, casseroles, marinades, and is a key ingredient in jerk seasoning. 
Baked goods: It adds a warm flavor to gingerbread, cakes, muffins, and pies. 
Other uses: It can be used in pickling, for flavor in mulled wine, and in fruit salads or compotes. 
Tips for use
Powerful flavor: A little goes a long way due to its pungency, so start with a small amount and add more to taste. 
Storage: Store ground allspice in an airtight container in a cool, dark place to maintain its freshness.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Tamarind Pulp
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Tamarind pulp is the sweet-sour, sticky flesh of the tamarind fruit, which grows inside a long pod. It has a tangy, date-like consistency and is often sold as a dehydrated block or wet, de-seeded form, ready to be soaked in water to create a paste for cooking. 
What it is
Source: It is the fibrous, tangy fruit that surrounds the seeds in a tamarind pod.
Flavor: It has a distinctively tart and fruity flavor that is often described as a mix of sweet and sour.
Texture: It is sticky and date-like in consistency, especially when it is sold as a compressed block. 
How it's sold
Blocks: Often sold as a dense, brown block of dehydrated, pressed pulp.
Pulp: Can also be found in a wet, often seedless, form.
Other forms: The fruit is also available as raw pods or as a liquid concentrate or powder.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Callaloo
ingredientsCatalog.description: Callaloo is a nutritious, leafy green vegetable popular throughout the Caribbean, often referring to the leaves of the amaranth plant or taro/dasheen (Xanthosoma), prepared in many ways, most famously as a stew or soup, but also steamed or sautéed as a side dish, rich in iron, vitamins, fiber, and minerals. It's a staple in Caribbean cuisine, a national dish in Trinidad and Tobago, and a beloved superfood offering health benefits like supporting immunity and bone health.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Jumbo Shrimp
ingredientsCatalog.description:
"Jumbo shrimp" refers to very large shrimp sold for food, typically around 13-15 shrimp per pound, and is also a common example of an oxymoron (a contradictory phrase) because "jumbo" means big and "shrimp" means small. While the term is a bit contradictory, it accurately describes large-sized crustaceans that are popular in dishes like cocktails, skewers, and seafood platters.  
Meaning in food & sizing
Size category: "Jumbo" is a marketing term indicating large shrimp, usually 13-15 count per pound, meaning fewer, larger shrimp fill a pound.
Count: The number per pound is key; smaller numbers (like 8/12 for colossal) mean bigger shrimp, while larger numbers (like 71/90 for small) mean smaller ones.
Usage: Jumbo shrimp are great for grilling or frying because their size holds up better to heat. 
Linguistic meaning
Oxymoron: The phrase is famous for being a humorous contradiction, as "jumbo" implies huge and "shrimp" implies small. 
Other uses
Sports: It's also the name of a Triple-A Minor League Baseball team, the Jacksonville Jumbo Shrimp.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Unsweetened Coconut Milk
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Unsweet Coconutmilk | Silk®Unsweetened coconut milk is a dairy-free, plant-based milk made from pressing coconut meat with water, containing no added sugars, and offering a pure, versatile, and slightly creamy liquid with natural coconut flavor, often fortified with vitamins like D and B12, and used in cooking, smoothies, coffee, and cereals. It's a healthier alternative to sweetened versions, focusing on natural ingredients like coconut, water, and sometimes a little salt or rice for texture. 
Key Characteristics
No Added Sugar: The defining feature, making it low in sugar and calories.
Dairy-Free: A popular substitute for cow's milk, suitable for vegans and those with lactose intolerance.
Versatile: Used in both sweet and savory dishes, from curries to smoothies.
Fortified: Many brands add calcium, Vitamin D, and Vitamin B12 for enhanced nutrition.
Ingredients: Typically contains coconut milk (coconut cream + water) and water, sometimes with a pinch of salt or rice. 
Types & Formats
Carton (Beverage): Thinner, lighter, and found in dairy aisles, great for drinking and cereal.
Canned (Culinary): Thicker, richer, used for cooking; available in full-fat or light versions.
Added Extras: Check labels for added stabilizers, gums, or sweeteners in some brands, though pure versions exist. 
How to Use
Drinks: Coffee, tea, smoothies, protein shakes.
Cooking: Curries, soups, sauces, baked goods (check fat content for baking).
Breakfast: Cereal, oatmeal, granola.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Fine Yellow Cornmeal
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Fine yellow cornmeal is dried yellow corn ground to a smooth, flour-like consistency, offering a mild sweetness and golden color, ideal for soft cornbread, muffins, pancakes, polenta, or as a light coating for fried foods, providing texture without grittiness. It's more refined than coarse meal, creating a softer crumb in baked goods, and is a versatile staple for various sweet and savory dishes, differing from coarse polenta or corn flour. 
Key Characteristics:
Texture: Finely ground, smoother than traditional coarse cornmeal, but not as powdery as wheat flour or cornstarch.
Flavor: Mildly sweet with a distinct corn taste.
Color: Golden yellow, from the yellow corn used.
Ingredients: Made from yellow dent corn, sometimes with the germ removed for a longer shelf life and finer texture. 
Common Uses:
Baking: Soft cornbread, muffins, quick breads, cakes.
Porridges/Cereals: Polenta (Italian-style) or creamy porridge.
Coatings: For frying fish or chicken to add a delicate crispness.
Other: Pancakes, hushpuppies, or added to recipes for richness. 
How it Differs:
From Coarse Meal: Creates a softer, less toothsome result.
From Corn Flour: While similar, "corn flour" can be even finer (like wheat flour), whereas fine cornmeal still has some texture.
From Masa Harina: Masa harina is cornmeal treated with lime (nixtamalization) for tortillas, while fine yellow cornmeal isn't.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Sweetened Condensed Milk
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Sweetened condensed milk is a dairy product made by evaporating about 60% of the water from cow's milk and then adding sugar to preserve it. This process creates a thick, rich, and very sweet liquid that is shelf-stable and used in a wide variety of desserts and baked goods, like cakes, pies, and candies. 
What it is
Concentrated milk: Most of the water is removed from the milk, making it much thicker than regular milk.
Added sugar: Sugar is added for sweetness and as a preservative, making the product shelf-stable until opened.
Rich flavor: The gentle heating process can also cause some natural sugars to caramelize, adding a deeper flavor. 
How it's used
Desserts and baking: It's a popular ingredient in many baked goods, such as cookies, brownies, cakes, and pies. It can also be used to make puddings, fudge, and candies.
Drinks: It can be used as a sweetener in coffee, tea, milkshakes, and cocktails.
Toppings and sauces: It can be used as a sauce or topping for other desserts. 
Key difference from evaporated milk
Evaporated milk: This is milk with most of the water removed but without added sugar. It has a thinner consistency and is not as sweet.
Sweetened condensed milk: This is essentially evaporated milk with a large amount of sugar added.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Orange Juice
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Orange juice (OJ) is a popular, vitamin C-rich liquid extracted from oranges, made by squeezing or pressing the fruit, available fresh or from concentrate, with pulp or without, and often fortified with calcium/vitamin D, serving as a refreshing drink that can support immunity and gut health. It's a key part of many diets, offering potassium, flavonoids, and other nutrients, though pure, unsweetened versions are best for health benefits. 
Key characteristics:
Source: Extracted from oranges (like Valencia, Navel, Blood oranges).
Production: Squeezed, sometimes reamed, processed (pasteurized for shelf life), filtered for pulp, or reconstituted from concentrate.
Varieties: Can be 100% juice, from concentrate, with pulp (bits) or pulp-free, or even fortified.
Nutrients: High in Vitamin C, potassium, folate, and flavonoids (like hesperidin).
Benefits: May boost immunity, support gut health (with pulp), reduce inflammation, and help with hydration. 
Types of OJ:
100% Juice: Pure extract with nothing added (no sugar, preservatives).
From Concentrate: Water is removed for storage and added back later.
Fortified: Calcium and Vitamin D are often added to commercial juices.
Probiotic: Some versions have beneficial bacteria added for gut health. 
How it's consumed:
As a standalone beverage.
In cocktails (like Screwdrivers, Tequila Sunrises).
As a cooking ingredient.

ingredientsCatalog.name: High Heat Cooking Oil
ingredientsCatalog.description: For high-heat cooking like searing, roasting, and deep-frying, use oils with a smoke point above 400°F (204°C), with top choices being Avocado oil, Peanut oil, Canola oil, Sunflower oil, and refined oils like safflower or rice bran, as they resist breaking down and smoking, ensuring better flavor and safety. Refined versions of oils like avocado and sunflower typically offer higher heat stability than their unrefined counterparts, though extra virgin olive oil can work for medium-high heat.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Seasoned Rice Vinegar
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Seasoned rice vinegar is regular rice vinegar that has been mixed with added sugar and salt, giving it a sweeter, more balanced flavor than unseasoned versions. It is a convenient condiment used to enhance dishes with a mix of sweet, salty, and tangy notes, and is commonly used for sushi rice, salad dressings, and dipping sauces. 
Key characteristics
Added ingredients: It is a blend of rice vinegar with added sugar and salt, and sometimes includes sake or MSG.
Flavor profile: The additions create a sweeter, more balanced, and less sharp taste compared to plain rice vinegar.
Uses: It is frequently used in cooking for sushi rice (also called sushizu), salad dressings, marinades, and as a dipping sauce for dumplings.
Convenience: Its convenience comes from being pre-seasoned, which saves the time of making your own mixture of sugar and salt for certain recipes. 
How to choose and use
Seasoned vs. unseasoned: Use seasoned rice vinegar when a recipe calls for added sweetness or when you want to make a quick, balanced dressing or sauce. Choose unseasoned rice vinegar if you prefer to control the exact amount of sugar and salt yourself.
Substitution: You can substitute it for unseasoned rice vinegar in a recipe, but the final dish will have a slightly sweeter and saltier result.
Making your own: You can easily make your own seasoned rice vinegar by heating regular rice vinegar with sugar and salt until dissolved, then letting it cool.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Napa Cabbage
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Napa Cabbage | Frieda's LLC - The Branded Produce CompanyNapa cabbage is a type of Chinese cabbage with a mild, sweet flavor and a tender, slightly crinkly texture that resembles romaine lettuce. It is a versatile vegetable used in many Asian dishes, such as soups, stir-fries, dumplings, and is a key ingredient in Korean kimchi. 
Characteristics
Appearance: It forms an oblong or oval head of tightly packed, pale green leaves with a thick, white stem. The inner leaves are often a pale yellow.
Flavor and texture: It has a mild, sweet flavor that becomes even sweeter when cooked. The texture is more delicate than regular cabbage, and it is crisp when raw.
Other names: It is also known as Chinese cabbage, celery cabbage (because of its white stalks), and sometimes wonbok. 
Uses
Cooking: Napa cabbage can be eaten raw or cooked and is used in a variety of dishes.
Soups and hot pots: It is a staple in many Asian soups and hot pot dishes.
Stir-fries: Its leaves soften nicely when stir-fried.
Dumplings: It can be chopped and used as a filling for dumplings.
Salads: Its crisp leaves are great for salads or slaws.
Pickling and fermenting: It is the main ingredient in traditional kimchi. 
Nutritional value
Napa cabbage is a good source of vitamins A, C, and K, as well as minerals like calcium, potassium, and magnesium.
It has a high water content, making it a low-calorie and hydrating choice.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Cilantro Leaves
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Cilantro leaves are the vibrant green, aromatic leaves and stems of the coriander plant (Coriandrum sativum), a member of the parsley family, known for its distinct pungent, citrusy, herbaceous flavor, essential in Mexican, Asian, and Latin American cuisines, often used fresh as a garnish or flavoring, while the plant's seeds are called coriander and used as a spice. 
Key characteristics:
Flavor: Strong, bright, and pungent; some people perceive it as soapy due to genetics.
Appearance: Delicate, flat leaves, similar to flat-leaf parsley.
Other names: Fresh coriander, Chinese parsley, Mexican parsley.
Culinary uses: Essential in salsas, curries, tacos, and soups, adding zest to both hot and cold dishes.
Plant distinction: "Cilantro" refers to the leaves, while "coriander" usually means the dried seeds, but the terms are often used interchangeably for the fresh herb.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Silken Tofu
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Silken vs. Regular Tofu: Know the DifferencesSilken tofu is a very soft, smooth, custard-like tofu with high water content, made by coagulating soy milk but leaving it unpressed, resulting in a delicate, jelly-like texture that doesn't hold its shape like firm tofu. Also called Japanese-style or soft tofu, it's perfect for blending into creamy vegan sauces, smoothies, desserts, dips, and soups, or for gentle heating in dishes like miso soup, but requires careful handling. 
Key Characteristics:
Texture: Extremely smooth, delicate, wobbly, and silky; almost liquid when not set.
Production: Made from soy milk, coagulated, but not pressed, retaining all its moisture.
Flavor: Mild, often described as neutral or slightly nutty, making it a great flavor carrier. 
Common Uses:
Creamy Bases: Blended for dairy-free cheesecakes, creamy pasta sauces, salad dressings, and vegan sour cream.
Soups: Gently heated and added to soups like miso soup or blended into creamy soup bases.
Desserts: Used as a base for custards, puddings, and smoothies.
Egg Substitute: Can be seasoned and crumbled for vegan scrambles.
Raw/Chilled: Eaten cold with savory dressings as an appetizer or side. 
How to Handle:
Delicate: It falls apart easily, so it needs gentle scooping or blending.
No Pressing: Do not press silken tofu; it will become watery and lose its unique texture.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Chinese Sesame Sauce
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Chinese sesame sauce, or zhima jiang (芝麻酱), is a rich, nutty, savory paste made from toasted sesame seeds, distinct from lighter Middle Eastern tahini by its deeper flavor from roasting and often coarser texture, used as a base for dips, dressings (like for Dan Dan noodles or cold vegetables), marinades, and hot pot sauces, blending savory soy sauce with vinegar, garlic, and sugar. 
Key characteristics:
Ingredients: Primarily toasted sesame seeds (white or black), but store-bought versions often add soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, water, and oils.
Flavor: Deeply nutty, savory, earthy, and slightly bitter, with varying sweetness depending on additions.
Texture: Thick and creamy, but often looser than pure tahini, designed to coat food well.
Variations: White sesame paste is common for savory dishes, while black sesame paste is often sweeter and used in desserts. 
Common uses:
Noodles: Drizzled over cold noodles (liangmian) or as the base for Dan Dan noodles.
Dips: For hot pot, dumplings, or steamed vegetables like eggplant.
Dressings: For salads, especially spinach (goma-ae) or cabbage.
Marinades: Mixed with soy sauce, garlic, and wine for grilled meats or chicken. 
How it differs from Tahini:
Toasting: Chinese sesame paste uses heavily toasted seeds for a more intense, aromatic flavor, while tahini uses untoasted or lightly toasted seeds.
Flavor Profile: Sesame paste is more assertive and nutty; tahini can be slightly more bitter and is the base for hummus.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Unsalted Beef Stock
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Unsalted beef stock is a rich, savory liquid made from simmering beef bones and meat with vegetables (like carrots, celery, onion) and herbs, but without any added salt, allowing cooks complete control over seasoning in dishes like soups, stews, gravies, and sauces. It provides a deep beef flavor base and often contains natural seasonings (like pepper, thyme) but no MSG or artificial flavors, making it a healthy, versatile cooking ingredient. 
Key Characteristics:
No Added Salt: The defining feature, letting you adjust saltiness to your recipe.
Rich Flavor: A concentrated beef taste from slow simmering.
Versatile Base: A foundation for many recipes, unlike broth (meat-based) which is often eaten alone.
Often Includes Veggies/Herbs: Contains natural flavor enhancers like onion, carrot, celery, bay leaf, and thyme, but no excess sodium. 
How It's Used:
Flavor Foundation: Adds depth to rice dishes, gravies, and braises.
Reheating: Adds moisture and flavor back to leftovers.
Ingredient Control: Ideal for low-sodium diets or recipes where you want to manage salt content precisely.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Shaoxing Wine
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Shaoxing wine (紹興酒) is a famous Chinese rice wine from Shaoxing, made from fermented glutinous rice, water, and wheat-based yeast, used for both drinking and cooking to add deep, complex, slightly sweet, and savory flavors to dishes like stir-fries, marinades, and braises, providing authentic restaurant taste. It's a key ingredient in Chinese cuisine, acting similarly to sherry or sake but with its unique profile, balancing fats and salt, and is known for its amber color and strong aroma.  
Key Characteristics & Uses:
Origin: Shaoxing, Zhejiang Province, China, with over 2000 years of history. 
Ingredients: Glutinous rice, water, and a wheat-based yeast (koji). 
Flavor Profile: Complex, nutty, slightly sweet, with a savory depth and sharp finish, but can be harsh when drunk straight due to added salt in cooking versions. 
Uses: Essential for marinades (drunken chicken), sauces, braised dishes, and stir-fries, adding umami and balancing flavors. 
Types: Comes in various grades, from dry (Yuan Hong) to sweet (Shaoxing). 
Gluten: Contains wheat, so not gluten-free. 
Substitutes:
Dry sherry, sake, or Chinese mirin (less sweet) can be used in a pinch, but won't replicate the exact flavor.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Mung Bean Sprouts
ingredientsCatalog.description: Mung bean sprouts are crisp, crunchy shoots grown from germinated mung beans, a popular legume in East and Southeast Asian cuisine, valued for their mild, nutty flavor and texture. They are white or ivory with small yellow-green leaves, high in water, fiber, vitamins (C, K, B), and minerals, and can be eaten raw in salads or cooked in stir-fries, soups, and noodles, offering a healthy, low-calorie addition to many dishes.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Chinese Long Beans
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Chinese long beans, also known as yardlong beans or snake beans, are long, slender legumes (related to black-eyed peas) with a mildly sweet, grassy flavor, used widely in Asian cooking for stir-fries, curries, and soups, valued for their crisp texture and ability to hold up well in cooking. They can grow very long (up to a yard) but are best harvested when pencil-thin, and unlike regular green beans, they are stringless and have a unique delicate taste. 
Key characteristics
Appearance: Very long (up to 3 feet), thin, cylindrical green pods with smooth skin.
Flavor: Grassy, slightly sweet, and earthier than common green beans, pairing well with strong spices.
Texture: Tender and crisp when young, remaining firm even after cooking, with no strings.
Botanical Family: A type of cowpea (Vigna unguiculata subsp. sesquipedalis). 
How to use them
Preparation: Trim the dry ends, then chop into 2-3 inch lengths.
Cooking: Excellent in stir-fries, curries, and deep-fried dishes.
Note: Don't overcook to avoid mushiness; they are great reheated. 
Where to find them
Asian markets, farmers' markets, and some supermarkets, often available year-round.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Dried Chillies
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Dried chillies are fresh chili peppers that have had their moisture removed through sun-drying, air-drying, or smoking, concentrating their vibrant color, intense heat, and complex, earthy, or fruity flavors, making them a staple spice in global cuisines for adding depth to dishes like moles, curries, and sauces. Unlike fresh, dried chillies offer a longer shelf life and transform into unique ingredients, with examples like smoky chipotles (smoked jalapeños) or rich, raisin-flavored Pasillas, notes Mextrade. 
Key Characteristics & Uses
Flavor Transformation: Drying brings out new tastes—sweet, smoky, fruity (like raisins), or chocolatey—that differ from the fresh pepper, notes Saveur and Don Day in SMA.
Heat Profile: Heat from dried chillies builds slowly and lingers, creating a deep, rich warmth rather than the immediate burst of fresh ones, says Asian Inspirations.
Preparation: They are often cleaned, stems and seeds removed (though sometimes left in), toasted, rehydrated in hot water, ground into powder, or blended into pastes and sauces.
Variety: Popular types include Ancho (dried poblano), Mulato (darker poblano), and Pasilla (rich, mild). 
Popular Examples
Chipotle: A smoke-dried jalapeño, intensely smoky and spicy.
Ancho: A sweet, mild, dried poblano with fruity notes.
Pasilla: Deep, rich flavor, often with raisin or plum notes, great in moles. 
In essence, dried chillies are versatile, flavour-packed ingredients that unlock a world of complex tastes in cooking.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Chicken Bouillon Powder
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Chicken bouillon powder is a concentrated seasoning made from dehydrated chicken stock, fat, and salt, along with other flavorings. It's a convenient way to add a rich, savory chicken flavor to dishes like soups, stews, sauces, and marinades, and can be used as a shortcut to make instant chicken broth by dissolving it in hot water. 
What it is
A dry powder made from concentrated chicken stock.
Often contains salt, chicken fat, and various seasonings and flavor enhancers, such as MSG, onion powder, and spices.
Available in powdered, granulated, or cube form. 
How it's used
As a seasoning: Adds a savory, umami-rich flavor to a wide range of dishes, including soups, stews, sauces, marinades, and stir-fries.
To make broth: Mix with hot water to quickly create an instant chicken broth.
As a finishing salt: Can be used as a seasoning for fried foods or vegetables. 
What to consider
Sodium content: Many types are high in sodium, so you may need to reduce the amount of other salt you add to a recipe.
Ingredients: Some brands may contain MSG or other additives, so check the label if you have dietary concerns. You can find brands that meet certain targets for salt and avoid specific allergens.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Egg Roll Wrappers
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Egg roll wrappers are thick, doughy wrappers made from wheat flour and eggs, designed to be deep-fried until golden, crispy, and chewy. They are distinct from the thinner wrappers used for spring rolls and are typically found in the refrigerated or frozen sections of grocery stores. Their main ingredients are flour, water, and eggs, along with salt and other additives for preservation. 
Characteristics and ingredients
Thick and chewy: Unlike the delicate skin of spring rolls, egg roll wrappers are noticeably thicker and have a chewier texture once cooked.
Pebbled texture: They often have a slightly rough or "pebbly" surface.
Key ingredients: The primary components are wheat flour, water, and eggs. Some variations may include other ingredients like salt, starches, or preservatives.
Preparation: They are usually fried, which causes them to blister and become crispy, but they can also be steamed.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Plum Sauce
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Plum sauce is a sweet and sour condiment, traditionally used in Cantonese cuisine, made from plums, sugar, vinegar, and spices like ginger and chili. It is a versatile sauce used as a dip for fried foods, a glaze for roasted meats, or a sauce for stir-fries. 
What it is
Flavor Profile: It has a complex, sweet, and tangy flavor that balances the palate.
Ingredients: The core ingredients are sweet plums, sugar, vinegar, and salt. Recipes often add ginger, chili peppers, and other spices or fruits like apple, peach, or apricot.
Appearance: It is a viscous, light-brown sauce. 
How it's used
Dipping Sauce: It's a classic dip for fried dishes like spring rolls, egg rolls, and deep-fried chicken balls.
Glaze or Basting Sauce: It can be used to coat and flavor roasted meats such as duck, pork, or chicken.
Stir-fry Sauce: It can be an ingredient in stir-fries or other cooked dishes.
Other Uses: It can also be drizzled over noodles, rice, or used as a dressing for salads. 
What it's not
Not Hoisin Sauce: Plum sauce is not the same as hoisin sauce. Hoisin is much darker, more savory, and has a fermented soybean base, whereas plum sauce is lighter in color and fruitier.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Chilli Bean Paste
ingredientsCatalog.description: Chilli bean paste, also known as Toban Djan or Doubanjiang, is a spicy, savory Chinese condiment made from fermented broad beans (fava beans) and chili peppers, often with soybeans, garlic, and salt, crucial in Sichuan cuisine for dishes like Mapo Tofu, offering a complex, umami, earthy flavor with a warming heat. It ranges in texture from chunky to smooth and deepens in flavor with age, developing a rich, deep red or purplish hue.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Snow Peas
ingredientsCatalog.description: Snow peas are a type of edible-pod pea with flat pods and undeveloped, tiny seeds inside, known for their crisp texture and subtly sweet flavor, often used in stir-fries or eaten raw; they are also called mangetout and harvested when young and tender, distinct from sugar snap peas which have rounder, thicker pods.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Pineapple Chunks
ingredientsCatalog.description: Pineapple chunks are thick, solid pieces of pineapple fruit, cut into cubes or irregular shapes, used in various dishes or enjoyed as a snack, but they are also famously known as retro, hard-boiled sweets (aka Pineapple Cubes) with a distinct pineapple flavor and a chewy center, popular in the UK

ingredientsCatalog.name: Pineapple Juice
ingredientsCatalog.description: Pineapple juice is a tangy, sweet, golden beverage made by pressing the liquid from fresh or canned pineapples, packed with Vitamin C, manganese, antioxidants, and enzymes like bromelain, used as a refreshing drink, cocktail base (like Piña Colada), or even as a meat tenderizer, known for its tropical flavor and potential anti-inflammatory properties.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Dried Shrimp
ingredientsCatalog.description: Dried shrimp are small, sun-dried shrimp with a concentrated, salty, and savory (umami) flavor, used as a flavor base in many Asian, African, and Latin American cuisines for dishes like stir-fries, soups, and pastes, often rehydrated before use but sometimes used whole or ground for snacks and seasonings. They come in various sizes, with larger ones often being higher grade and smaller ones used whole, imparting intense seafood flavor to dishes.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Buckwheat Flour
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Buckwheat flour is a nutritious, naturally gluten-free flour milled from the triangular seeds of the buckwheat plant, related to rhubarb, not wheat, known for its earthy, nutty, slightly sour flavor, perfect for pancakes (like French galettes), noodles (soba), and as a wheat flour substitute in baking for added protein and fiber. 
Key Characteristics
Gluten-Free: Ideal for celiac diets or gluten-free baking.
Flavor Profile: Distinctive earthy, nutty, and slightly bitter taste.
Nutrient-Rich: High in protein, fiber, and minerals, with antioxidants.
Appearance: Greyish-brown, sometimes with dark flecks from the hull. 
Uses in Cooking & Baking
Traditional Dishes: Famous for French galettes (savory pancakes) and Japanese soba noodles.
Pancakes & Waffles: Adds moisture and flavor, often blended with other flours.
Baking Substitute: Can replace a portion of wheat flour in breads, cakes, and pastries, providing a protein boost. 
How it's Made
Milled from the whole buckwheat seed, with only the inedible husk removed, retaining nutrients.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Split Peas
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Split peas are dried, hulled, and split halves of field peas (the same plant as fresh peas) that cook quickly and creamy, offering a nutritious, high-protein, high-fiber pulse, available in green (sweeter) and yellow (milder) varieties, commonly used in soups and stews. 
Key characteristics
Origin: They are mature peas harvested, dried, and then split in half along their natural seam.
Types: Green split peas are sweeter, while yellow split peas are milder and starchier.
Cooking: Their split form means they cook much faster and don't require pre-soaking, turning soft and creamy.
Nutrition: Rich in protein, fiber, potassium, and iron, making them very healthy and economical.
Uses: Famous for split pea soup, they're also great in dahls, casseroles, and vegetable dishes. 
How they differ from fresh peas
Fresh peas are eaten young and tender, while split peas are mature, dried, and processed for long storage and different culinary uses.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Ground Sugar
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Ground sugar refers to sugar that has been milled into a fine powder, most commonly known as powdered sugar, icing sugar, or confectioners' sugar, used for frostings, glazes, and dusting; it's typically granulated sugar blended with a small amount of starch (like cornstarch) to prevent caking and create a smooth, clump-free texture, essential for baking and decorating. 
Types of Ground Sugar
Powdered/Icing Sugar: Granulated sugar ground extremely fine, usually with added starch (cornstarch) for anti-caking, perfect for smooth frostings and dusting.
Caster Sugar (Superfine Sugar): A finer grind than regular granulated sugar, dissolving more quickly, ideal for meringues, syrups, and delicate cakes.
Free-Flowing Brown Sugar: A less moist, powdered version of brown sugar that pours easily and is great for oatmeal or cereal toppings. 
How It's Made & Used
Homemade: You can make your own by grinding granulated or caster sugar in a blender or coffee grinder until powdery, then sifting it.
Uses: Creates smooth icings, glazes, fillings for pastries, and adds a delicate finish to desserts.
Key Ingredient: The anti-caking agent (starch) is crucial for its texture and workability in recipes, preventing it from hardening or clumping.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Speculaas Spice Mix
ingredientsCatalog.description: Speculaas spice is a warm, fragrant blend of ground spices, primarily cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, ginger, and cardamom, with common additions like aniseed, white pepper, coriander, and mace, creating the distinctive flavor for Dutch/Belgian speculaas cookies (or speculoos) enjoyed during holidays. It offers a sweet yet spicy profile, perfect for autumn baking, but is versatile enough for desserts and even savory dishes, with recipes varying slightly by baker, much like pumpkin pie spice but unique.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Almond Paste
ingredientsCatalog.description: Almond paste is a thick, spreadable baking ingredient made from finely ground almonds, sugar (often equal parts or slightly more almonds), and a binder like egg whites, corn syrup, or water, giving it a slightly coarse, nutty texture. It's a versatile filling for pastries (croissants, tarts), cookies, cakes, and even chocolates, distinct from smoother, sweeter marzipan because of its higher almond content and coarser texture, making it less pliable for decorative molding.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Dutch Stroop
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Dutch stroop (pronounced "strohp") simply means syrup in Dutch, but it refers to a specific, thick, caramel-like syrup made from sugar beet or cane sugar, used as the sweet, gooey filling in the famous stroopwafels, or syrup waffles, which are two thin waffles sandwiched together with this rich filling. Traditionally, stroop has a deep, molasses-like flavor, offering a complex sweetness rather than just pure sugar, and it's perfect for warming over a hot drink to soften.  
Key Characteristics of Stroop:
Source: Traditionally derived from sugar beet syrup or reduced treacle, sometimes with added brown sugar and fructose. 
Flavor: Rich, deep, slightly tangy, and malty, distinct from standard caramel. 
Texture: Thick, sticky, and gooey when warm. 
Stroopwafels (Syrup Waffles):
Origin: Invented in Gouda, Netherlands, centuries ago. 
How to Eat: The classic way is to place a stroopwafel on top of a hot cup of coffee or tea for a few minutes, allowing the heat to soften the stroop filling, creating a gooey, delightful treat. 
In essence, stroop is the essential sweet heart of the beloved stroopwafel, providing its signature texture and flavor.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Coconut Oil
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Coconut oil is an edible oil extracted from the kernel or meat of matured coconuts, widely used in cooking, cosmetics, and industry. It is composed of 80–90% saturated fat, specifically high in medium-chain fatty acids like lauric acid. It is solid at room temperature and liquid above 
 (

Key Aspects of Coconut Oil:
Types: Virgin (or Extra Virgin) is extracted from fresh meat without chemicals; Refined is processed from dried coconut meat (copra).
Uses: Used for cooking (baking, sautéing), as a moisturizer for skin/hair, and in oil pulling for oral hygiene.
Health Considerations: While it contains Medium-Chain Triglycerides (MCTs), which are processed quickly by the body, its high saturated fat content can increase LDL cholesterol, the American Heart Association (AHA) warns.
Nutritional Properties: It contains antioxidant polyphenols, particularly in virgin varieties. 

Coconut oil is a popular alternative for cooking, providing a distinct flavor, though it should be used in moderation.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Vegetable Millk
ingredientsCatalog.description:
Vegetable milk, commonly known as plant-based milk, is a dairy-free, lactose-free beverage made from water-extracted extracts of legumes, nuts, seeds, or cereals. These popular dairy alternatives—such as soy, almond, oat, and coconut milk—are chosen for vegan, allergy-friendly, or sustainable diets and are frequently fortified with calcium and vitamins. 
Key Aspects of Vegetable Milk:
Production: It is made by grinding plant materials (nuts, seeds, grains) and mixing them with water. The mixture is then filtered to remove sediment, creating a fluid that resembles dairy milk.
Common Types:
Soy milk: Highest protein content, closely resembling cow’s milk, but a major allergen.
Almond milk: Low in calories and high in vitamin E.
Oat milk: Known for a creamy texture and higher fiber content.
Coconut milk: Known for its rich, creamy texture.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Dessert Rice
ingredientsCatalog.description: Dessert rice, often referred to as "pudding rice" in the UK, is a short- or medium-grain white rice used to create creamy, sweet dishes like rice pudding. It is characterized by a high starch content that releases during cooking, thickening milk into a custard-like consistency. Common varieties include Arborio.This video shows how to make a classic, creamy rice pudding:

ingredientsCatalog.name: Nougatine
ingredientsCatalog.description: Nougatine is a crunchy French confection made by caramelizing sugar and mixing it with chopped or sliced nuts, typically almonds. It is a thin, hard, caramel-based brittle often used to add texture to desserts, pastries, and chocolates. It is distinct from soft nougat, as it contains no egg whites or honey.Key Characteristics and UsageComposition: Primarily caramelized sugar and toasted nuts (almonds, hazelnuts, or sometimes sesame).Texture & Taste: Thin, very crunchy, and brittle with a rich, caramelized nutty flavor.Usage Examples:Garnish/Topping: Crushed and sprinkled over creams, mousse, and cakes for crunch.Shapes: Molded into cones, discs, or cylinders while still warm to serve as vessels for mousse or ice cream.Chocolates: Used as a brittle filling coated in chocolate.Snack: Enjoyed on its own at coffee time.Preparation: Sugar is cooked until caramelized, then combined with nuts. It must be rolled out rapidly while hot between parchment paper or silicone mats (Silpat) before it hardens.Synonyms and Related TermsFrench Brittle: Often described as a type of nut-based brittle.Caramelised Roasted Nuts: A common description for the preparation method.Nut Brittle: A more general term for this type of candy.It is important to work with nougatine quickly once made, as it sets very rapidly and can be softened again briefly in the oven at low temperatures ((140-150^{circ}C)) if needed.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Ground Turmeric
ingredientsCatalog.description: Ground turmeric is a vibrant yellow-orange spice produced by boiling, drying, and grinding the root (rhizome) of the Curcuma longa plant. It is renowned for its earthy, peppery, and ginger-like flavour, commonly used in curries, stews, marinades, and yellow mustard to provide both intense color and warm flavor.Key Characteristics and Uses:Flavor Profile: It has a strong, earthy, slightly bitter taste with hints of ginger and pepper.Coloring Agent: Due to its high pigment, it is used to give dishes like rice, soups, and cauliflower pickles a bright yellow color.Key Ingredient: It is a key ingredient in curry powders, spice blends, and popular for making "[golden milk" (turmeric tea or lattes).Main Compound (Curcumin): The active ingredient is curcumin, which is known for its strong antioxidative and anti-inflammatory properties.Culinary Uses: It is versatile for use in savory dishes, such as fish curries, marinades for poultry, and vegetable dishes.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Ground Walnuts
ingredientsCatalog.description: Ground walnuts (also known as walnut flour or meal) are whole walnuts processed into a fine, consistent powder. They are highly valued for gluten-free and keto baking, adding a rich, nutty flavor, moisture, and healthy Omega-3 fats to recipes.Key CharacteristicsFlavor & Texture: They offer a creamy, robust nutty flavor and impart a tender, moist crumb to baked goods.Nutrition: Naturally high in plant-based protein, dietary fiber, and essential fatty acids.Dietary Friendly: Naturally gluten-free and very low in carbohydrates, making them a great wheat flour alternative.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Light Raisins
ingredientsCatalog.description: Light raisins, commonly known as golden raisins or sultanas, are dried seedless grapes treated with sulfur dioxide. This treatment preserves their bright colour and gives them a soft, plump texture with a fruity, slightly tangy flavour.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Mung Beans
ingredientsCatalog.description: Mung beans (Vigna radiata) are small, oval, olive-green legumes native to India. Known for their slightly sweet and nutty flavor, they are an extremely versatile and nutrient-dense food packed with plant-based protein, dietary fiber, and essential vitamins.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Dried Dill
ingredientsCatalog.description: Dried dill (or dill weed) is the dehydrated, fern-like leaves of the dill plant. It offers a milder, slightly sweet flavor with notes of aniseed and grass. Because the drying process reduces its potency, it has a longer shelf life and requires larger quantities than fresh dill.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Strained Yoghurt
ingredientsCatalog.description: Strained yoghurt is regular yoghurt that has been filtered to remove most of its liquid whey. This ancient technique results in a much thicker, creamier texture and a slightly tarter taste. Because the whey is removed, it is more concentrated, packing more protein and less lactose than unstrained yoghurt.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Pickled Grape Leaves
ingredientsCatalog.description: Pickled grape leaves are tender, young grape vine leaves that are preserved in a salt brine or diluted vinegar. They are pliable, soft, and have a distinct tangy, slightly briny flavor. They are most famous for being the outer wrapper in Mediterranean and Middle Eastern stuffed dishes, such as dolmas

ingredientsCatalog.name: Morning Glory
ingredientsCatalog.description: Morning glory in food refers to a green leafy vegetable commonly known as water spinach (or ong choy). Celebrated for its juicy, leafy tops and long, crisp, hollow stems, it is a staple in Southeast Asian and Chinese cuisines. It is typically stir-fried with garlic, chili, and savory sauces

ingredientsCatalog.name: Tempura Flour
ingredientsCatalog.description: Tempura flour is a specialized, low-protein wheat flour often blended with starches (like corn or tapioca starch) and leavening agents. It is designed to create a thin, airy, and incredibly crispy coating for deep-fried seafood and vegetables without absorbing excess oil

ingredientsCatalog.name: Rice Flour
ingredientsCatalog.description: Rice flour is a fine, powdery flour made by finely milling raw rice. It is naturally gluten-free and serves as a popular wheat flour substitute in baking, a thickening agent for soups and sauces, and a coating for frying

ingredientsCatalog.name: Wheat Flour
ingredientsCatalog.description: Wheat flour is a powdery baking staple made by grinding milled wheat grains. It is the foundation for a wide variety of foods—from breads and pastries to pastas and pizza crusts—and is primarily categorized by its gluten protein content and how much of the wheat kernel is used

ingredientsCatalog.name: Kampot Pepper
ingredientsCatalog.description: Kampot pepper is a premium, highly prized variety of Piper nigrum cultivated exclusively in the Kampot and Kep provinces of Cambodia. Renowned in culinary circles as the "king of pepper," it features a deep, complex flavor with intense spice, floral and citrus notes, and a hint of eucalyptus.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Beef Tenderloin
ingredientsCatalog.description: Beef tenderloin is the most tender and prized cut of beef, famous for its buttery texture and lean profile. Taken from the non-weight-bearing psoas major muscle along the cow's spine, this muscle gets almost no exercise, which yields exceptionally soft meat

ingredientsCatalog.name: Sticky Rice Flour
ingredientsCatalog.description: Glutinous rice flour is a finely milled flour made from ground, dehydrated glutinous (sticky or sweet) rice. Despite its name, it does not contain gluten. The term "glutinous" refers to the glue-like, chewy, and sticky consistency it takes on when cooked

ingredientsCatalog.name: Pandan Leaves
ingredientsCatalog.description: Pandan leaves come from a tropical plant (Pandanus amaryllifolius) native to Southeast Asia. Known as the "vanilla of the East", these long, bright green leaves are used to add a sweet, floral, and subtly nutty aroma to both sweet and savory dishes.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Taro
ingredientsCatalog.description: Taro (Colocasia esculenta) is a starchy tropical root vegetable recognized by its hairy brown skin and white flesh speckled with purple. It is highly versatile and is used in a wide variety of sweet and savory dishes globally

ingredientsCatalog.name: Longan
ingredientsCatalog.description: The longan (Dimocarpus longan) is a small, round tropical fruit closely related to the lychee. Native to Southeast Asia and southern China, its name literally translates to "dragon's eye" in Chinese because its translucent, juicy white flesh and hard black seed resemble an eyeball when peeled

ingredientsCatalog.name: Coconut
ingredientsCatalog.description: A coconut is the edible fruit of the coconut palm (Cocos nucifera), which grows in tropical climates. Botanically, it is classified as a "drupe" (a stone fruit like a peach), but it acts as a versatile source of food, drink, oil, and fiber.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Pickled Scallion Heads
ingredientsCatalog.description: Pickled scallion heads are the crisp, white bulbous bases of scallions or similar bunching onions, preserved in a sweet, sour, and salty brine. They are beloved for their intense crunch and zesty tang, cutting through rich, savory foods.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Pickled Scallion Head Brine
ingredientsCatalog.description: Pickled scallion head brine is the acidic, seasoned liquid used to cure and preserve the bulbous white and light green bases of scallions (green onions) or spring onions. It imparts a crisp, tangy, and slightly sweet flavor to the onions while softening their sharp bite

ingredientsCatalog.name: Kaffir Lime
ingredientsCatalog.description: The kaffir lime (also widely known as the makrut lime) is a knobby, dark green citrus fruit native to Southeast Asia. While the juice and zest are occasionally used in traditional cooking, the glossy, hourglass-shaped leaves are the most prized part of the plant, acting as an essential aromatic in Thai, Cambodian, and Indonesian cuisines.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Kaffir Lime Leaves
ingredientsCatalog.description: Kaffir lime leaves (also known as makrut lime leaves) are the aromatic, glossy green leaves of the kaffir lime tree. Often described as the "bay leaf" of Southeast Asia, they are a staple in Thai, Vietnamese, and Indonesian cooking. They are prized for their intense, citrusy, and slightly floral fragrance

ingredientsCatalog.name: Plantain
ingredientsCatalog.description: The word "plantain" most commonly refers to a starchy, green, cooking fruit closely related to the banana. In a separate, botanical context, it also refers to a common wild weed

ingredientsCatalog.name: Tapioca
ingredientsCatalog.description: Tapioca is a starch extracted from the root of the cassava plant, a tuber native to South America. It is virtually pure carbohydrate and is naturally gluten-free. Because of its neutral flavour and gelling properties, it is commonly used to thicken soups, bake gluten-free goods, and make chewy desserts.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Sour Pork Sausage
ingredientsCatalog.description: Sour pork sausages are primarily traditional fermented sausages (like Thai Naem or Lao Som Moo) that get their distinct tangy flavor through natural lactic acid fermentation. Alternatively, in Western cooking, the term can refer to standard pork sausages flavored with a sweet-and-sour glaze

ingredientsCatalog.name: Pickled Garlics
ingredientsCatalog.description: Pickled garlic is fresh garlic cloves preserved in an acidic brine (usually vinegar, salt, and water). The pickling process completely transforms the allium: it softens the cloves and mellows the harsh, pungent bite of raw garlic, replacing it with a sweet, tangy, and slightly savory flavor profile.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Hot Mint
ingredientsCatalog.description: "Hot mint" most commonly refers to Vietnamese coriander (Persicaria odorata), an aromatic herb widely used in Southeast Asian cooking. It is also known by its Vietnamese name rau răm or as laksa leaf.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Vegetables
ingredientsCatalog.description: A vegetable is any edible part of a plant consumed by humans, such as the roots, stems, leaves, flowers, or seeds. It is a culinary classification rather than a strict biological one, and vegetables are typically eaten as part of a savory meal.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Unsalted Peanuts
ingredientsCatalog.description: Unsalted peanuts are standard peanuts (technically ground-based legumes) that have been processed or left raw without any added salt. They deliver the pure, earthy, and naturally nutty flavor of the legume, making them a heart-healthy, versatile snacking and cooking option

ingredientsCatalog.name: Corn On The Cob
ingredientsCatalog.description: Corn on the cob is a culinary term for a cooked ear of sweet corn (maize) served with the kernels still attached to the central core (the cob). It is typically boiled, steamed, or grilled, and usually eaten directly off the cob, often seasoned with butter and salt.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Grapefruit
ingredientsCatalog.description: A grapefruit is a large, subtropical citrus fruit that is a natural hybrid between a sweet orange and a pomelo. Known for its segmented flesh and distinctively tart, sweet, and slightly bitter flavor, it comes in several varieties with colors ranging from pale yellow to dark ruby red.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Mango
ingredientsCatalog.description: A mango is a sweet, tropical stone fruit (drupe) native to South Asia, grown on large evergreen trees. Known globally as the "king of fruits", it has smooth, vibrant skin (ranging from green to yellow, red, or orange) and juicy, golden-orange flesh surrounding a large, flat central pit.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Ground Mahleb
ingredientsCatalog.description: Ground mahleb (also known as mahlab, mahlepi, or mahlep) is an aromatic baking spice made from the seed kernels of the St. Lucie cherry (Prunus mahaleb). Once extracted from the hard cherry pits, the seeds are ground into a fine powder that tastes like a fragrant blend of bitter almond, marzipan, and cherry.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Tobasco Sauce
ingredientsCatalog.description: Tabasco is an iconic American brand of hot sauce famous for its signature tangy, spicy flavor. Created in 1868 on Avery Island, Louisiana, the original sauce is made from just three simple ingredients: tabasco peppers, vinegar, and salt, which are aged in oak barrels for up to three years

ingredientsCatalog.name: Smoked Ham
ingredientsCatalog.description: Smoked ham is a cut of pork from the hind leg that has been cured (soaked in a saltwater brine or dry-rubbed) and then slow-cooked over smoldering wood chips to impart a distinct smoky flavor. It is available either fully cooked (ready to eat) or partially cooked

ingredientsCatalog.name: Parsnips
ingredientsCatalog.description: A parsnip is a root vegetable closely related to the carrot and parsley. It features a pale, cream-colored, carrot-like shape and offers a sweet, nutty, and earthy flavor that intensifies when cooked.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Lamb Fat
ingredientsCatalog.description: Lamb fat is the natural adipose tissue found in sheep. It has a rich, earthy flavor and can be used in its raw form, melted down, or rendered into a shelf-stable cooking fat called tallow.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Grits
ingredientsCatalog.description: What they are: Crushed kernels from a starchy type of corn called dent corn.Texture & Taste: They are thicker and grainier than oatmeal, with a mild, earthy corn flavor that acts as a blank canvas.Hominy Grits: Many grits are made from hominy, which is corn soaked in an alkali solution (like lye) to remove the tough outer hull before grinding

ingredientsCatalog.name: Shatkora
ingredientsCatalog.description: Shatkora (also known as satkora or hatkhora) is a fragrant, wild citrus fruit native to the Sylhet region of northeastern Bangladesh. Resembling a knobby, thick-skinned orange or lime, it is prized for its highly aromatic, tangy, and slightly bitter flavor, and is primarily used to elevate heavy meat curries.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Beef Shoulder
ingredientsCatalog.description: Beef shoulder—often referred to in the meat industry as the chuck—is a flavorful, economical, and hardworking cut from the front of the cow. Because the cow uses these muscles constantly, it is tough and well-exercised, making it ideal for "low and slow" cooking methods like braising or stewing

ingredientsCatalog.name: Panch Poran
ingredientsCatalog.description: Panch phoran (meaning "five spices" in Bengali) is a traditional whole-seed spice blend from Eastern India, Bangladesh, and Nepal. Unlike most spice mixes, the seeds are never ground; they are used whole to add a crunchy texture and complex flavor to dishes.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Daikon Radish
ingredientsCatalog.description: Daikon radish (also known as mooli) is a large, mild-flavored winter root vegetable that looks like a long, white carrot. Native to East Asia, it has a crisp texture, juicy flesh, and a subtly sweet, slightly peppery flavor. It is highly versatile and can be enjoyed raw, cooked, or pickled

ingredientsCatalog.name: Date Molasses
ingredientsCatalog.description: Date molasses (also known as date syrup) is a thick, dark, velvety syrup made from concentrated date juice. It has a natural, deep, caramel-like sweetness with a slightly fruity, treacle-like flavor.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Breadfruit
ingredientsCatalog.description: Breadfruit (Artocarpus altilis) is a large, starchy tropical fruit belonging to the mulberry and jackfruit family. Named for its potato-like, bread-like texture and aroma when cooked, it is a highly versatile staple food in the Pacific Islands and other tropical regions.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Ground Mustard
ingredientsCatalog.description: Dry mustard (also known as mustard powder or ground mustard) is a fine, yellow powder made by grinding dried mustard seeds. It is highly concentrated and possesses a pungent, tangy heat when mixed with liquid, making it a staple ingredient in rubs, marinades, salad dressings, and cheese sauces

ingredientsCatalog.name: Banana Leaves
ingredientsCatalog.description: Banana leaves are the large, flexible, and waterproof fronds of the banana plant. Because they are not edible (due to high fiber content), they are primarily used across tropical regions in South/Southeast Asia, Latin America, and the Caribbean for cooking, serving, and eco-friendly packaging

ingredientsCatalog.name: Pigs Trotters
ingredientsCatalog.description: Pig trotters, also known as pig's feet or pettitoes, are the culinary term for the lower part of a pig's legs, from the ankle down. They are highly prized in many global cuisines for their rich collagen content, which breaks down during slow cooking into a succulent, gelatinous texture

ingredientsCatalog.name: Red Pepper Sauce
ingredientsCatalog.description: Red pepper sauce is a versatile, vibrant condiment or cooking base made primarily from roasted or cooked red bell peppers. It is known for its sweet, smoky, and savory flavor profile, and is used globally in a variety of cuisines

ingredientsCatalog.name: Evaporated Milk
ingredientsCatalog.description: Evaporated milk is a shelf-stable, canned dairy product made by heating regular cow’s milk to remove about 60% of its water content. This process concentrates the milk, resulting in a thick, creamy texture and a slightly caramelized flavor, but—crucially—contains no added sugar

ingredientsCatalog.name: Ground Onion
ingredientsCatalog.description: Ground onion generally refers to a dried, powdery seasoning made from dehydrated onions. However, the exact meaning depends on whether you are using a dried spice from the pantry or following a recipe.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Sirop De Liège
ingredientsCatalog.description: Sirop de Liège (or Luikse siroop in Flemish) is a traditional Belgian fruit spread. Resembling a thick, dark, and sticky apple butter, it is made by slowly cooking, straining, and reducing apples, pears, and sometimes dates until it becomes a concentrated, caramel-like paste

ingredientsCatalog.name: Frogs Legs
ingredientsCatalog.description: Frog legs are the muscular hindlimbs of frogs consumed as a culinary delicacy in various global cuisines, most notably in France, China, Indonesia, and the American South. Prized for their tender texture and mild flavor, they are frequently compared to a cross between chicken and white fish

ingredientsCatalog.name: Pork Cheeks
ingredientsCatalog.description: Pork cheeks are the small, intensely flavorful muscles located in the hollow of a pig's cheek, just beneath the eyes. Because the pig uses these muscles constantly, the meat is very lean but loaded with connective tissue, yielding a melt-in-the-mouth texture when slow-cooked

ingredientsCatalog.name: Pumpkin Puree
ingredientsCatalog.description: Pumpkin puree is simply cooked, blended pumpkin flesh. It has a smooth, creamy texture and a mildly sweet, earthy flavor. Often sold in tins, it is a versatile base for both sweet baked goods (like pies, cakes, and muffins) and savory dishes (like soups and sauces

ingredientsCatalog.name: Black Eyed Peas
ingredientsCatalog.description: Black-eyed peas are a highly nutritious, pale cream-colored bean with a distinct black spot that resembles an eye. Despite the name, they are actually a legume belonging to the cowpea family, rather than a true pea. They have a nutty, earthy flavor and are a dietary staple worldwide

ingredientsCatalog.name: Palm Hearts
ingredientsCatalog.description: Heart of palm is a crisp, white vegetable harvested from the inner core and growing bud of certain palm trees (such as coconut or açaí). It is highly prized for its delicate, slightly nutty flavor, which resembles that of an artichoke heart, and is commonly enjoyed in salads, pastas, or as a vegan meat substitute.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Summer Savoury
ingredientsCatalog.description: Summer savory (Satureja hortensis) is a highly aromatic annual herb belonging to the mint family. Known historically as the "bean herb", it has a delicate, peppery flavor with notes of thyme and marjoram and is a staple in both traditional European and Canadian cooking

ingredientsCatalog.name: Cottage Cheese
ingredientsCatalog.description: Cottage cheese is a fresh, soft, and mild-tasting dairy product made from cow's milk curds mixed with a creamy dressing. It is unaged and known for its distinct "pebbled" texture, featuring small or large curds suspended in a loose, creamy liquid.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Red Curry Paste
ingredientsCatalog.description: Thai red curry paste (phrik kaeng phet) is a versatile, flavorful blend of herbs, spices, and dried red chilies that serves as the aromatic foundation for many Thai dishes. It offers a rich, slightly smoky, and gently spicy profile, making it a staple for curries, stir-fries, and marinades

ingredientsCatalog.name: Prahok
ingredientsCatalog.description: Prahok is a traditional Cambodian fermented fish paste made from salted, crushed, and fermented river fish. Acting as a foundational ingredient in Khmer cuisine, it is prized for its pungent aroma—often earning it the nickname "Cambodian cheese"—and its deep, savory umami flavor.Because it is intensely salty and strong, it is rarely eaten on its own, but rather used as a seasoning or a condiment.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Glutinous Rice
ingredientsCatalog.description: Glutinous rice—also known as sticky rice or sweet rice—is a variety of Asian rice characterized by opaque grains and a highly chewy, sticky texture when cooked. It is distinct from other rices because it consists almost entirely of a starch called amylopectin and contains virtually zero amylose.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Mung Bean Paste
ingredientsCatalog.description: Mung bean paste is a sweet or savory legume-based purée made from hulled, split yellow mung beans. It has a mildly nutty, slightly vanilla-like flavor and a rich, velvety texture often compared to marzipan. It is a highly popular ingredient in Asian desserts and pastries.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Conchs
ingredientsCatalog.description: A conch (/kɒŋk/ or /kɑːntʃ/) is a large marine sea snail with a thick, spiral-shaped shell. The term also refers to the shell itself, which is widely known for its use as a musical instrument, in cultural traditions, and as a popular seafood delicacy

ingredientsCatalog.name: Beets
ingredientsCatalog.description: Beets are vibrant, nutrient-dense root vegetables known for their earthy, sweet flavor and distinct deep-red or golden color. Both the root itself and the leafy greens attached to them are edible, packed with essential vitamins, fiber, and powerful antioxidants.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Cassava
ingredientsCatalog.description: Cassava is a starchy root vegetable native to South America, also widely known as yuca, manioc, or mandioca. A primary staple food for over 800 million people, it thrives in tropical and subtropical regions and is prized for its drought resilience and high calorie content.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Crab Meay
ingredientsCatalog.description: Crab meat is the edible, soft, and naturally sweet flesh extracted from the body, legs, and claws of a crab. Highly valued in global cuisines, it is prized for its delicate texture, bright appearance, and high protein content.The flavor and texture vary significantly depending on the part of the crab and the species:

ingredientsCatalog.name: Lobster
ingredientsCatalog.description: A lobster is a large marine crustacean with a hard shell, a long muscular tail, eight legs, and two large claws. It is highly prized as a culinary delicacy, though its shell turns bright red only when cooked.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Palm Butter
ingredientsCatalog.description: Palm butter is a rich, creamy West African sauce and stew base made from the mashed pulp of boiled palm oil fruit. It features a deep orange-red color and a nutty, earthy flavor, and is most famously used in Liberian and Sierra Leonean cuisine to make a savory, protein-packed stew

ingredientsCatalog.name: Zapallo Squash
ingredientsCatalog.description: Zapallo is the generic Spanish term used in many South American countries for various types of winter squashes and pumpkins. Similar to butternut squash or calabaza, it features a tough rind and dense, sweet, and nutty orange flesh. It is a highly versatile vegetable frequently used in hearty stews, soups, and purées.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Panquehue Cheese
ingredientsCatalog.description: Panquehue is a popular semi-soft, creamy, and mild cow's milk cheese from the Aconcagua Valley of Chile. Reminiscent of European Tilsit, it is frequently blended with chives or traditional Chilean spices like Merkén (smoked chili pepper)

ingredientsCatalog.name: Swiss Cheese
ingredientsCatalog.description: Swiss cheese is a mild, slightly sweet, and nutty cow's milk cheese famous for its iconic holes (or "eyes"). In North America, the term refers to any cheese modeled after the traditional Swiss Emmental. In the UK and Europe, it usually describes alpine-style cheeses sourced directly from Switzerland

ingredientsCatalog.name: Great Northern Beans
ingredientsCatalog.description: Great Northern beans are medium-sized white beans known for their delicate, nutty flavor and firm texture. Because they hold their shape well when cooked, they are a staple in chilis, casseroles, and hearty stews.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Lima Beans
ingredientsCatalog.description: Lima beans (Phaseolus lunatus) are flat, moon-shaped legumes known for their mild, creamy texture and slightly nutty flavor. Often called butter beans (especially in the US South and the UK), they come in both small ("baby limas") and large varieties, and are eaten either young and green or fully mature and white

ingredientsCatalog.name: Banana Pepper
ingredientsCatalog.description: Banana peppers are a mild, tangy member of the chili pepper family. Named for their bright yellow color and elongated, curved shape, they offer a subtle sweetness and a mild crunch. They range from 0 to 500 on the Scoville scale, making them roughly five times milder than a standard jalapeño

ingredientsCatalog.name: Farmers Cheese
ingredientsCatalog.description: Farmer’s cheese is a mild, unripened white cheese made by curdling milk and draining the liquid whey. It typically has a crumbly texture and a subtle, milky, slightly tangy flavor. The name generally refers to two distinct styles of cheese:

ingredientsCatalog.name: Habanero Pepper
ingredientsCatalog.description: The habanero is a highly pungent, lantern-shaped chili pepper famous for its intense heat and fruity, floral aroma. Ranging from 100,000 to 350,000 Scoville Heat Units, it is roughly 12 to 140 times hotter than a jalapeño and is a staple in Mexican, Central American, and Caribbean cuisines

ingredientsCatalog.name: Sazon Goya With Azafran
ingredientsCatalog.description: Sazón Goya with Azafrán is a popular Latin seasoning blend used to add bright golden color and savory flavor to foods. "Azafrán" means saffron in Spanish. This seasoning mix is a cheap and easy way to give your meals a rich, yellow color.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Achiote Seeds
ingredientsCatalog.description: Achiote seeds (also called annatto seeds) are small, red-orange seeds from the achiote tree (Bixa orellana). They are native to tropical parts of the Americas. People use them as a natural food coloring and a spice to add earthy, slightly peppery flavours to food.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Queso Fresco
ingredientsCatalog.description: Queso fresco (Spanish for "fresh cheese") is a mild, soft, and slightly crumbly white cheese made from cow's milk (or a mix of cow and goat). Native to Mexico, it is a staple of Latin American cuisine, frequently crumbled over tacos, enchiladas, and salads to provide a creamy, salty, and milky contrast to spicy dishes.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Alinos Sauce
ingredientsCatalog.description: Aliños sauce is a popular, fresh vegetable seasoning paste used in Latin American cooking, especially in Colombia. Cooks blend fresh ingredients like peppers, onions, garlic, and cilantro into a liquid base. Families use it as a flavorful starter base for soups, stews, beans, and meat marinades

ingredientsCatalog.name: Raw Yucca
ingredientsCatalog.description: The term "raw yucca" typically refers to the untreated starchy root vegetable (more accurately spelled yuca or cassava). It must never be eaten raw. It contains toxic cyanogenic compounds that require careful peeling and thorough cooking to neutralize.However, "Raw Yucca" is also a popular brand of 100% natural powdered yucca extract (derived from the Yucca schidigera plant) used in gardening and hydroponics.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Flank Steak
ingredientsCatalog.description: Flank steak is a lean, flavorful cut of beef from the cow's lower abdominal muscles. Known for its intense beefy taste, it is long, flat, and features thick muscle fibers running in one direction. Because it is a hardworking muscle, it can be tough and is best marinated and cooked quickly over high heat

ingredientsCatalog.name: Achiote Paste
ingredientsCatalog.description: Achiote paste—also known as recado rojo—is a vibrant, earthy seasoning staple in Mexican, Central American, and Caribbean cooking. It is made primarily from ground annatto seeds, blended with garlic, vinegar, and warm spices like cumin, cloves, and oregano. The paste gives dishes like cochinita pibil a signature peppery flavor and brilliant red hue.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Salsa Lizano
ingredientsCatalog.description: Salsa Lizano is a ubiquitous Costa Rican condiment originally created in 1920. Similar in color, usage, and consistency to Worcestershire sauce or HP Sauce, this light brown, slightly sweet and savory sauce is vegetable-based (made with ingredients like carrots, onions, and cucumbers) and features a mild blend of spices without the heat. It is the defining ingredient in Costa Rica's national dish, gallo pinto.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Maria Cookies
ingredientsCatalog.description: Maria cookies (known as galletas María in Spanish) are thin, round, lightly sweet biscuits embossed with intricate edges and a central name. Made simply with wheat flour, sugar, and vegetable oils, they have a mild vanilla flavor and a crisp texture that makes them perfect for dunking in tea or coffee.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Cafe La Llave
ingredientsCatalog.description: Café La Llave is a popular brand of dark-roasted, Latin-style espresso coffee. Rooted in Cuban heritage, the intensely aromatic ground coffee is widely used in households and at "ventanitas" (coffee walk-up windows) to make rich, concentrated beverages like cafecitos or cortaditos

ingredientsCatalog.name: Pimento Stuffed Olives
ingredientsCatalog.description: Pimento-stuffed olives are pitted green olives filled with a sliver of sweet red pimento pepper. This classic pairing balances the olive's natural bitterness and salty brine with the pepper's mild sweetness. They are most famous as the iconic garnish for classic gin and vodka martinis.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Ground Black Pepper
ingredientsCatalog.description: Ground black pepper is a spice made from dried, unripe peppercorns (the fruit of the Piper nigrum vine) that have been milled into a fine powder or coarse granules. Prized for its heat—driven by the compound piperine—and earthy, floral notes, it is a global staple used to season both sweet and savory dishes.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Cuban Bread
ingredientsCatalog.description: Cuban bread is a long, baguette-like white bread characterized by its thin, crispy crust and soft, airy interior. It uniquely incorporates a small amount of fat, traditionally pork lard, to yield a tender crumb, and is traditionally baked on top of a palm frond to create a natural split.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Deli Ham
ingredientsCatalog.description: Deli ham is precooked, cured, or smoked pork from the hind leg, sliced thin for sandwiches, wraps, and salads. Sold at deli counters or in pre-packaged sections, it ranges from whole-muscle cuts to reformed processed meat and comes in varieties like honey-baked, hickory-smoked, and Black Forest.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Yuca
ingredientsCatalog.description: Yuca (pronounced yoo-cuh)—also known as cassava or manioc—is a starchy, edible tuber native to South America and widely grown in tropical climates. It is a dietary staple for hundreds of millions of people worldwide and serves as the source of tapioca

ingredientsCatalog.name: Cooking Apples
ingredientsCatalog.description: Cooking apples (also known as culinary apples) are apple varieties grown primarily for cooking rather than eating raw. They are typically larger, firmer, and tarter than dessert (eating) apples. When exposed to heat, their higher acidity provides a sharp flavor, and their cellular structure breaks down perfectly into a smooth, frothy puree

ingredientsCatalog.name: Vanilla Powder
ingredientsCatalog.description: Vanilla powder (or vanilla bean powder) is a dry, concentrated baking ingredient made by drying and grinding whole vanilla beans—including the pods and seeds—into a fine powder. It provides a pure, intense vanilla flavor and classic black specks without the alcohol or moisture found in liquid extracts.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Coarse Salt
ingredientsCatalog.description: Coarse salt is a category of edible salt with large, chunky grains rather than fine granules. It is primarily used to provide a distinct, crunchy texture to foods, for creating salt crusts on meats, or for grinding fresh seasoning at the table

ingredientsCatalog.name: Rye Grain
ingredientsCatalog.description: Rye is a hardy cereal grain related to wheat and barley, primarily known for its use in dark breads, crispbreads, and whiskey. It is celebrated for its rich, earthy flavor and high nutritional profile, boasting significant amounts of fiber, B vitamins, and protein.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Dark Beer
ingredientsCatalog.description: A dark beer is any beer that gets its deep amber, brown, or black color from roasted grains. Instead of being heavy or high in alcohol by default, many dark beers are surprisingly crisp and drinkable. They offer complex, roasted flavors like chocolate, caramel, and coffee.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Seeds
ingredientsCatalog.description: In botany, a seed is the embryonic stage of a plant's life cycle, enclosed in a protective outer covering. It develops from a fertilized ovule and contains three primary parts: a tiny dormant plant (embryo), stored food (endosperm), and a tough protective coat (testa

ingredientsCatalog.name: Rye Flour
ingredientsCatalog.description: Rye flour is a nutrient-dense powder milled from the rye kernel (a grain related to wheat and barley). It has a distinct earthy, nutty flavor and is famously used to bake dense, chewy breads (like pumpernickel or sourdough)

ingredientsCatalog.name: Dried Sorrel
ingredientsCatalog.description: Dried sorrel typically refers to the dehydrated, deep-red calyxes of the Hibiscus sabdariffa plant (often called roselle). When steeped in water, it produces a ruby-red, tart beverage that tastes similar to cranberry or pomegranate and is heavily used in festive Caribbean drinks, teas, and punches.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Sorrel Jam
ingredientsCatalog.description: Sorrel jam is a sweet and tart preserve made from the vibrant red calyxes (petals) of the sorrel plant (also known as hibiscus sabdariffa or roselle). It is highly popular in the Caribbean, particularly around Christmas, and is often made by sweetening and cooking down the leftover pulp after boiling sorrel for drinks.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Codfish Bulljaw
ingredientsCatalog.description: "Codfish bulljaw" (often spelled buljol) is a popular Caribbean salad made from shredded salted cod, fresh tomatoes, onions, peppers, and olive oil. Originating in Trinidad and Tobago, the name stems from French patois and is commonly served for breakfast with fried dumplings called "bakes" or crusty bread

ingredientsCatalog.name: Farine
ingredientsCatalog.description: Farine (derived from the Portuguese farinha or French for flour) primarily refers to a toasted, granular meal made from the cassava root. It is a staple food in many South American and West African communities, often compared to grits or cream of wheat, and is valued for being gluten-free and highly shelf-stable

ingredientsCatalog.name: Cassava Flour
ingredientsCatalog.description: Cassava flour is a gluten-free, grain-free flour made from the entire root of the cassava plant (also known as yuca or manioc). The root is peeled, dried, and ground into a fine powder. With its mild, neutral taste and powdery texture, it is a popular, highly versatile 1:1 substitute for wheat flour in baking and cooking

ingredientsCatalog.name: Ice Cubes
ingredientsCatalog.description: An ice cube is a small, typically rectangular or square piece of frozen water used to chill beverages. They are made by freezing water in mechanical refrigerators using trays or automated makers.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Cocoy Banana
ingredientsCatalog.description: A "cocoy" banana is a local name in Dominica for a stubby, creamy banana. Also known globally as the burro banana (in Mexico) or saba (in the Philippines), this variety is shorter and thicker than the standard Cavendish, with a slightly tangy, starchy, and lemony flavor.Because it is not as sweet as regular bananas, it is rarely eaten raw. Instead, it is a versatile cooking staple.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Green Papaya
ingredientsCatalog.description: Green papaya is simply the unripe, raw version of the standard papaya fruit. Unlike the sweet, orange-fleshed fruit you are used to, green papaya has firm, white flesh with a crisp texture and a very mild, neutral taste similar to a cucumber or jícama

ingredientsCatalog.name: Sweet Quark
ingredientsCatalog.description: Sweet quark usually refers to Fruchtquark or Topfencreme, a creamy, protein-rich dairy product popular in Germany and Austria. It is a slightly sweet version of plain quark, which is a fresh, unaged cheese with a texture and taste similar to a cross between Greek yogurt and sour cream

ingredientsCatalog.name: Sour Milk
ingredientsCatalog.description: Sour milk can refer to raw milk that has naturally fermented via lactic acid bacteria, or pasteurized milk artificially "soured" with an acid like lemon juice or vinegar. In baking, it acts as a substitute for buttermilk—the acid reacts with baking soda to help baked goods rise

ingredientsCatalog.name: Canned Beans
ingredientsCatalog.description: Canned beans are fully cooked, shelf-stable legumes that are blanched and sealed in metal cans with water, salt, and sometimes preservatives. Because they require no soaking or boiling, they are a highly convenient and budget-friendly pantry staple used for quick meals, salads, stews, and dips.

ingredientsCatalog.name: Gingerbread Spice
ingredientsCatalog.description: Gingerbread spice is a warm, aromatic blend of ground spices commonly used in holiday baking. It is more ginger-forward than similar blends like pumpkin pie spice and gets its classic festive flavor and fragrance from a combination of ground ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, and cloves

ingredientsCatalog.name: Ground Chicken
ingredientsCatalog.description: Ground chicken is raw chicken that has been finely chopped or minced, usually using a meat grinder or food processor. It is made from a mix of chicken meat (either breast, thighs, or a blend of both), and is often sold plain or with skin left on depending on the desired fat content

meals.name: 15-minute chicken & halloumi burgers
meals.instructions:
STEP 1

Put the chicken breasts between two pieces of baking parchment and use a rolling pin to gently bash them until they are approximately 1cm thick. Cut each chicken breast into two even pieces.

STEP 2

If you're using a frying pan, heat two frying pans over medium-high heat, with one of them containing oil. Fry the chicken in the oiled pan for 3-4 mins on each side until they are cooked through. Season the chicken, reduce the heat, drizzle in the chilli sauce and half of the lemon juice, and cook for an additional 1-2 mins until the sauce is reduced. Remove the chicken from the heat.

STEP 3

If you're using an air-fryer, preheat it to 180C for 4 mins. Add the chicken to the air-fryer and cook for 12 mins. Drizzle over the chilli sauce and half the lemon juice and cook for an additional 1-2 mins until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is reduced. Remove the chicken and keep it warm.
STEP 4

While the chicken is cooking, toast the buns in the dry frying pan for 30 seconds. Transfer them to a plate. If you're using an air fryer, put the buns in the air fryer for 1-2 mins until they are warm. Increase the air fryer temperature to 200C.
